## This document is to practice reading data in R

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidyverse)

data_raw <- read.csv(
  "data/db_hiscod_csv_v1_en.csv",
  sep = ";",
  header = TRUE
)

```
### Make a copy of the data
```{r}
data_copy <- data_raw |>
  separate_wider_delim(
    cols = 1,
    delim = ";",
    names = strsplit(names(data_raw)[1], ";")[[1]]
  )
```

### Take a look of the data
```{r}
head(data_copy)
colnames(data_copy)
```
### The column I am interested in are id, year, contry_name, women_participation. So I am slecting the three column to check the dataset. 
```{r}
data_select <- 
data_copy |> 
  select(id, country_name, year, women_participation)
```

### For contry, I only want to include France; for year i want to range from 1700 to 1900
```{r}
france_data <-data_select |>
    filter(
    country_name == "France",
    year >= 1700,
    year <= 1900
  )
head(france_data)
```


### Check the distribution of women's participation
```{r}
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(france_data, aes(x = women_participation)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Women's Participation in French Social Conflicts",
    x = "Women's participation",
    y = "Number of events"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
### write a test for checking the country is France and the year range from 1700 to 1900
```{r}
# Simulated dataset matching your actual data
test_data <- tibble(
  id = 1:4,
  country_name = c("France", "France", "Germany", "France"),
  year = c(1789, 1850, 1800, 1690),
  women_participation = c("Unknown", "No", "Yes", "Yes")
)

# Filter France and years 1700–1900
test_result <- test_data |>
  filter(country_name == "France", year >= 1700, year <= 1900)

# Test the filter
stopifnot(nrow(test_result) == 2)
stopifnot(all(test_result$country_name == "France"))
stopifnot(all(test_result$year >= 1700 & test_result$year <= 1900))

```
